title: Normalization of an equivariant projective generic model is an alteration
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $S$ and $C$ be integral projective finite-type $k$-schemes, and put $K=k(S)$. Let $J$ be a finite group acting compatibly on $k$, $S$, and $C$ by field and scheme automorphisms; neither action is required to be faithful. Let $p:C	o S$ be an equivariant $k$-morphism and assume a specified identification
$$C	imes_S\operatorname{Spec}K\simeq\operatorname{Spec}M$$
for a finite extension $M/K$, identifying $k(C)$ with $M$. Let $
u:W=C^
u	o C$ be the normalization in $k(C)$ [def-sc-normalization]. Then $
u$ is finite, surjective and birational; $W$ is normal integral and projective of finite type over $k$; and
$$W	imes_S\operatorname{Spec}K\simeq\operatorname{Spec}M,\qquad k(W)=M,$$
with the identifications induced by $
u$. Each automorphism $g$ of $C$ in the given action has a unique lift $\widetilde g$ to $W$ with $
u\widetilde g=g
u$. These lifts form a $J$-action on $W$, semilinear for the given action on $k$, inducing on $M$ exactly the action coming from $C$. The composite $b=p
u:W	o S$ is equivariant, admits a closed immersion $W\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ for some $n\geq0$, is proper and surjective, and is finite over a dense open subscheme of $S$. In particular $b$ is an alteration. Normal means all local rings are integrally closed domains, birational means an isomorphism of function fields, and an alteration here means proper, surjective and finite over a dense open between integral schemes.

Field, integral scheme, projectivity in the global closed-embedding convention, finite type, function field, finite extension, fibre product, normalization, finite morphism, surjectivity, closed immersion, properness and open immersion use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-sc-normalization], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Agent assembly of Tag 0BXR lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic and Tag 0GK4 lemma-normalize-projective; action lifting: morphisms.tex Tag 035Q lemma-normalization-normal (4); generic finiteness: morphisms.tex Tag 0BAI lemma-finite-over-dense-open.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-model-functoriality] to V=C and the identity finite extension k(C)/k(C). The identification with the given normalization follows from [def-fin-normalization-extension]. Thus W is normal integral of finite type over k, W and C are Noetherian, nu is finite surjective, and k(W)=k(C)=M via nu. This last equality makes nu birational in the convention of the statement. Apply [lem-fin-finite-over-projective] with base Spec k, T=C and Y=W. Its affine-base clause gives a global closed immersion W into a finite projective space over k; the base is Noetherian because a field has only the ideals (0) and (1).

source.place: varieties.tex Tags 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic) and 0GK4 (lemma-normalize-projective); affine-base finite-over-projective clause

proof.text: Since C is integral, its componentwise normalization is exactly W: there is only the reduced component C itself, by [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization] and [def-sc-normalization]. Apply [lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-generic-properties] to the Noetherian scheme C. Its generic-fibre clause says W times_C Spec k(C) is canonically Spec k(C). The given map C times_S Spec K = Spec M to C is the generic-point map under k(C)=M. Associativity of fibre products therefore gives W times_S Spec K = W times_C Spec M = Spec M. These are the maps induced by nu, so the field identification is the one in step 1.

source.place: morphisms.tex Tag 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), Tag 0BXC (lemma-normalization-birational); generic fibre and associativity

proof.text: Apply the isomorphism-functoriality clause of [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-model-functoriality] to each automorphism of the data (k,C,k(C),k(C)); it supplies compatible lifts preserving identities and compositions, hence the semilinear J-action on W and its specified function-field action. Uniqueness even among lifts not supplied with field data follows from [lem-sfb-component-dominant-normalization-lift] applied to g nu:W to C: W is normal integral, C is Noetherian, and g nu is dominant since nu is surjective and g is an automorphism. In particular nu composed with the lift equals g nu. With a left action on functions the convention is inverse pullback on both C and W, so nu identifies their actions on M exactly.

source.place: morphisms.tex Tag 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), part (4); semilinear integral-closure functoriality

proof.text: Since S is projective over k, [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] makes S proper and hence separated over k. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-constant-projective-graph] with F=k, R=W and c=b=p nu to obtain the closed immersion W into a finite projective space over S, with structural map b. The extension k/k has degree one. The same graph lemma gives properness of b. Equivariance is the equality b lift(g)=p g nu=g p nu, using the given equivariance of p and step 3.

source.place: morphisms.tex Tag 0C4Q (lemma-projective-permanence), closed-graph proof; projective implies proper

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], S is Noetherian, since it is of finite type over the spectrum of the Noetherian field k. Properness makes b finite type and universally closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Its generic fibre from step 2 is nonempty, so the closed image of b contains the generic point of integral S and is all of S. The generic point of integral W maps to that of S, and the residue-field extension is M/K, finite by hypothesis. Apply (i) implies (ii) of [lem-per-generic-fibre-finiteness-criterion] to b to obtain a dense open over which b is finite. Together with properness and surjectivity this is precisely the stated alteration condition.
